why:
Summed panel scores across all five criteria and three judges: case-study 125 (ECD 42, prospect 41, producer 42), parallel-journey 113 (38 / 40 / 35), canvas 97 (33 / 31 / 33). Case-study has the best total, and it also leads explains_what_was_built (27 against 22 and 21) and feasibility. It loses premium_and_real to parallel-journey, so this plan keeps case-study's skeleton: numbered chapters, short independent takes, the 112.5 BPM grid, the phone-to-desktop finder handoff and full coverage of the build. It then fixes every fatal flaw the judges named.

1. Too much text. There are now seven short statements, each one or two lines and 11 words or fewer, plus one event-synced line. There are no support lines, the labels are short ('01 — HOME'), and there are two motion chips instead of three ms annotations. Every statement stays readable for at least 1.9 s, except T6, whose shot is one bar between cuts 2 and 3 (about 1.5 s).
2. Cormorant beside The Seasons. Orbit's voice is now General Sans and Cabinet Grotesk only, both already in app/fonts. The client's serif appears only inside the real pages.
3. Keynote grammar (locked camera, devices sliding in on cue, five cuts). The devices are now fixed objects on one Linen table and only the camera moves: a pull-back, two trucks and a final pull-back, all eased, with lean of 2° or less and screen speed of 1,500 px/s or less. There are 3 hard cuts instead of 5. Each one lands on a bar downbeat and is a change of camera setup motivated by on-screen action: a match cut on the product, a chapter cut, and the finder handoff.
4. The −7° tabletop arc is gone. The finale is a flat pull-back.
5. Different products in the bag (prospect). From the 8.0 s click and tap onward the phone and the desktop both buy Raw Seduction, EGP 970, and both meters were verified live on the owner's updated site: 'EGP 1,220 away', then 'EGP 121 away' on the phone after the Enzo 1898 suggestion, and 'EGP 250 away' on desktop after +1. Before 8.0 s the two screens show different heroes on purpose: the desktop opens on the site's hero film, the phone on the Instagram-ad landing pinned to Raw Seduction's still.
6. The producer's build issues. Motion blur now follows one rule: a 180° shutter (±1/120 s) of 9 triangular-weighted taps while anything moves, with the screens cross-fading between their recorded frames (240 Hz for the fast-scrolling takes, 120 Hz for the rest), and a single sample at rest or when a click or tap switches the page inside the shutter. The IntersectionObserver is flushed every frame with real rAFs. The cursor is driven with page.mouse along the logged path, and paths run through card and chip gutters so only the intended elements hover. Image routing is set per take, against verified local files. There is no edge bleed: every device is fully in frame or fully out.

From parallel-journey: the continuous camera on a lit stage, desktop and phone acting in call and response, the URL pill showing the path only, the studio voice in General Sans, the large 'Orbit' signature on the final chord, the honest credit line and click pans that follow the device. Its double finder is replaced by case-study's handoff. From canvas: the line synced to an on-screen event, the inspect-style chip, the cursor sprite read from the computed CSS cursor, and the URL pill updating live. Both of canvas's flaws are avoided: no third-party fragrance name ever appears (the captures hide every 'Inspired by' line, and Raw Seduction, an Eternal Original, has none), and every click really navigates.

Every coordinate and string used in this plan was checked against the running production build on localhost:3000 on 2026-10-09, and re-checked against the owner's updated site on 2026-10-10.

title: eternal — a storefront by Orbit (case study, 30 s, desktop and phone)
logline: One storefront runs live on two screens set on a Linen table. The site opens itself with its own loader, whose curtain lifts on the home page's hero film, while the phone holds the Instagram-ad first screen, pinned to Raw Seduction's still. The desktop browses into the eterno catalogue; from there both land on Raw Seduction and add it to the same bag, a sheet on the phone and a drawer on desktop. The scent finder starts on the phone and finishes on desktop from the link. The camera then pulls back to both screens on the three matches and 'Designed and built by Orbit.' Short numbered statements explain each part, on an original 112.5 BPM track the picture is cut to.
rules: Every pixel inside a device is the production build (next start on localhost:3000) captured frame-exactly on a virtual clock. The film draws nothing inside the screens except the cursor and touch marks.
No CG objects, no void, no bloom, particles, light shafts, chromatic aberration, vignette, glow wipes, fly-throughs or LUT. Site pixels are composited 1:1 in sRGB with no grade.
Devices are fixed physical objects on one Linen table and never slide, fade or scale on their own. Only the camera moves, and only between the five framings defined in visual_system.
Exactly 3 hard cuts (12.800, 21.333, 23.467), each on a bar downbeat and each a change of camera setup motivated by on-screen action. There are no dissolves.

Every change of picture inside a screen is the site's own behaviour. It either starts with the page itself (the loader's mark and curtain, the hero words, and the home hero film, which starts once the page is idle and plays on the virtual clock) or is triggered by a visible click, tap or scroll: PageFade, header switch, line hover, FLIP re-flow, card hover, sticky bar, sheet, drawer, meters, finder slide, composing mark and the results swap.

A device may change page off-frame only if that change is never shown: the desktop during bars 7–8 and 11, the phone during bars 5–6 and from the bar-12 cut until the final pull-back brings it back (about 26.0). Every join between takes is hidden off-frame or falls on a cut: D1 runs as one take from the loader to the card click, so no join shows on screen.

Overlays sit only on clean Linen, never over a page or a device. Each enters on a beat with the site's rise (16 px, 600 ms, ease-emphasized) and has fully left 0 ms or more before the camera move or cut that would cross it.

Overlay copy comes only from the verified claims list: no metrics, no '43', no reviews, no launch or live-domain claim, no third-party fragrance names, no timelines, and no credit for the client's identity, photography or film.
Faces: General Sans Regular and Cabinet Grotesk Regular from app/fonts only. Never The Seasons (demo licence, missing glyphs) and never Cormorant.

Capture hygiene in every take: fresh context, consent cookie, eternal.loaded set (except D1), never an Instagram/FBAN/FBAV UA, utm parameters only on P1 (the phone's ad landing, the one take where html[data-ad] is set), reducedMotion 'no-preference', .wa-float hidden, carets transparent, scroll-behavior auto, Shopify images routed to the product's own local photos, and every 'Inspired by <third-party>' line hidden. Only those lines are hidden: 'Eternal Original' labels and 'Not inspired by another fragrance: only at eternal.' stay visible.

Scrolls run on the live viewport: a sine-eased scrollTo with behavior 'instant' per recorded frame (240 Hz in D1 and P2, 120 Hz in the other takes). They are never wheel scrolls and never full-page strips, because the header switch, parallax, sticky bar and reveals are scroll-driven.

The pointer moves only along logged paths through gutters (the column gutters x 382–406, 708–732 and 1034–1058, the gap between the chip row and the first card row, the right gutter x 1360–1440), so only the intended elements hover. Phones are driven with page.tap only.
The beat grid is 112.5 BPM: beat = 16 frames, bar = 64 frames. Clicks and taps land on beats or half-beats, and site timers (450, 280 and 600 ms) fall where they really fall.
Both devices are large whenever they are in frame: desktop at 0.79–0.81 css scale in SPLIT and DESK, phone at 0.94 in SPLIT and 1.07–1.09 in PHONE. WIDE (0.66) is used only under the end card.

Motion blur is a 180° shutter, ±1/120 s around each output frame. While anything moves it takes 9 taps with triangular weights, for camera and site motion alike, and the screens cross-fade between their recorded frames. A single sample applies at rest, or when a click or tap switches the page's state inside the shutter. Before F(128) the desktop shows D1 at the frame's own time, so the hero film's 24 fps frames never double-expose. No tap reaches across a cut. Frame 0 is bare Linen.
visual_system:
FRAME: 1920×1080, 30 fps, 900 frames. Master H.264 High 4:2:0, tagged BT.709 for primaries, transfer and matrix, limited range.

STAGE: one infinite Linen #F3EFE7 table. Stage units equal output px at camera k=1.
- Light: a broad, soft Paper #FAF8F3 radial falloff from the upper left, fixed to the stage, at most +2% luminance at the hot spot. Camera moves therefore reveal a real surface, not a flat fill.
- Grain: monochrome dither at σ ≈ 1.2/255, re-seeded per frame, over the whole frame. It is only there to stop banding.
- Forbidden: vignette, bloom, particles, light shafts, chromatic aberration and any colour grade.

FIXED LAYOUT on the table (stage px):
- Browser window: x 120–1254, y 281–1030. The chrome bar is y 281–321 (40 px). The viewport is y 321–1030, 1440×900 css at 0.7875.
- Phone body: x 1407–1800, y 166–1030, 418×919 css at 0.94. Screen inset 13, status bar 44, viewport 367×793.
- Gap between the devices: 153 px.
- Both devices lie in the table's plane: under lean the whole table turns as one, with no separate parallax.

FRAMINGS. The camera is a centre (cx, cy) in stage px, a zoom k, and a lean in rotateY with 2400 px perspective. A solver keeps on-screen boxes within ±1 px of the positions below.
- OPEN: k 2.20, centre (687,675). The frame lies wholly inside the desktop viewport and the loader mark draws at about 222 px.
- SPLIT: k 1.00, centre (960,540). Desktop on screen at x 120–1254, y 281–1030. Phone at x 1407–1800, y 166–1030. Text band at y 72–255, x 120–1254.
- DESK: k 1.00, centre (390,655). Desktop at x 690–1824, y 166–915. Phone fully off frame to the right. Text column at x 120–610.
- PHONE: k 1.14, centre (2132,598). Phone at x 134–582, y 48–1032, about 1.07 css scale. Desktop fully off frame to the left (its right edge at −41). Text column at x 700–1720.
- WIDE: k 0.66, centre (514,568). Both devices at x 700–1809, y 275–845. Credit column at x 120–620.

CAMERA RULES:
- Moves use log-scale zoom with the centre path coupled to the zoom.
- Trucks ease in and out on a sine curve. Screen speed peaks at about 840 px/s (SPLIT→DESK) and about 1,230 px/s (PHONE→SPLIT), always 1,500 px/s or less.
- Lean is up to 2° into the direction of travel, only while moving, and back to 0 at rest.
- Holds drift no more than 1.5% scale and 12 px per bar, so no frame is frozen.
- Velocity is continuous everywhere except at the three cuts. tools/path.mjs verifies this.

MOTION BLUR AND SHARPNESS:
- Site takes are recorded at 240 Hz where the page moves fast (D1 and P2, the takes with scrolls under the camera) and at 120 Hz elsewhere.
- The shutter is 180° at 30 fps: each output frame gathers ±1/120 s. While anything moves it takes 9 taps across that span with triangular weights, each with its own camera pose, and the screens cross-fade between their two nearest recorded frames, so camera and page motion both blur instead of strobing.
- A single sample applies when everything holds still, or when a click or tap switches the page's state inside the shutter (a real 30 fps capture shows one side or the other).
- Before F(128), D1 shows the take at the frame's own time, so the hero film's 24 fps frames never double-expose and the loader's curtain stays crisp.
- No tap reaches across a cut. Frame 0 is bare Linen: the loader's first paint (a dot where its stroke will start) lasts 4 ms on the site, so the desktop's screen is blank for that one frame.
- Desktop takes are captured at a true DPR 2: the CDP screenshot clip is scaled to the DPR (without it CDP returns css-pixel shots). They show at no more than 1.73 px per css px (OPEN), so they are always supersampled.
- Phone takes are captured the same way at a true DPR 3 and show at no more than 1.09 px per css px.
- Takes are pre-scaled with Lanczos3 into two mip levels: on desktop, full size (2880 px) for the loader's close framing (D1 through film 2.2) and 1440 px wide for everything else; on the phone, 488 px wide (1.25 px per css px).

INPUT MARKS (the only things drawn over UI):
- Desktop cursor: an arrow or a hand, chosen per frame from the logged computed cursor. Night fill with a 1.5 px Linen outline and a soft drop shadow, drawn at about 35 css px (1.45× life size, so it reads at film size). It moves along the page.mouse path, interpolated between logged positions, and scales to 0.92 for the press (mouse down to mouse up). It rests in the right gutter while not in use.
- Phone touch mark: a 44 css px two-tone disc, so it reads on Linen pages and on dark photographs alike: a Linen fill at 30%, a 1.5 px Linen ring inside the edge, a thin 1 px Night outer ring and a soft shadow. It appears 150 ms before the tap, fading in over 100 ms and scaling from 0.85 to 1, so it lands on the control and not on the page the tap opens. It holds 100 ms after the tap, fades over 240 ms, and sits on the logged tap point.

COLOUR: the encode is checked after decoding. A Linen patch and a Night UI patch must both be within ΔE<2.

ANIMATION, the site's own tokens:
- In: each line rises 16 px while fading in, over 600 ms on ease-emphasized, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1). Lines stagger by 80 ms in the order label, statement lines, synced or detail line. READABILITY:

transition_grammar:
1) CAMERA, NOT SLIDES. The devices are props fixed on one table, and the only things that move them on screen are camera moves between five framings. There are four camera moves, each motivated by something on screen:
- The pull-back out of the loader (0.8–2.133), motivated by the curtain lifting.
- The truck from SPLIT to DESK (8.533–9.600), following the desktop's click into the catalogue.
- The pull-back from PHONE to SPLIT (17.067–18.667), motivated by the sheet opening and leading to the same bag on desktop.
- The final pull-back from DESK to WIDE (25.600–27.400), as the matches land and the work is shown whole.
Moves start on bar downbeats. Trucks use a sine ease-in-out and pull-backs land with zero velocity. Lean is 2° or less, only while moving, and screen speed is 1,500 px/s or less. Between moves the camera drifts by 1.5% or less per bar and is never frozen.

2) THREE HARD CUTS, all on bar downbeats and all changes of camera setup (coverage, not slides):
- 12.800 (bar 7), DESK to PHONE: a match cut on the product. The desktop clicks Raw Seduction and the page fades; we cut to the phone, already on Raw Seduction from its hero tap at 8.267.
- 21.333 (bar 11), SPLIT to PHONE: the chapter cut into the finder, on the swell where the kick drops out.
- 23.467 (bar 12), PHONE to DESK: the handoff. The URL pill shows the phone's answers carried in the link.
There are no other cuts and no dissolves, wipes, glows or fly-throughs.

3) THE SITE'S OWN TRANSITIONS change everything inside the screens: the G1 loader curtain, the home hero film (its 1.2 s fade-in over its poster, then the intro and the loop), G2 PageFade at 200 ms, the header switch, the line-still crossfade, the FLIP re-flow, the card hover, the sticky bar (240 ms), the bag sheet and the drawer (320 ms ease-emphasized), the meters (600 ms), the finder screen slide (320 ms), the composing mark and the finder's own hard swap to results. Each starts with the page or is triggered by a visible click, tap or scroll, and each is captured on the virtual clock and never retimed.

4) CALL AND RESPONSE. When both screens are in frame, one acts and the other answers half a beat or one beat later (8.000 desktop, then 8.267 phone; 19.733 phone, then 20.267 desktop). Two inputs never land in the same beat.

5) TYPE follows the camera. Text enters on a beat once its zone is clear and has fully left before any move or cut crosses that zone. Chips appear on the first frame of the animation they name.

6) SOUND marks only real events: clicks and taps panned to the device's on-screen position, two air brushes under the sheet and the drawer, swells into the downbeats of bars 3, 7, 11, 13 and 14, a felt note on the bar-12 cut, and the final chord under 'Orbit'. Camera moves get no whooshes.

captures.method:
Virtual clock (timers, rAF, requestIdleCallback, performance.now, Date.now and media playback) plus CDP playback rate 0 and getAnimations stepping, at 240 Hz because its scrolls are fast.

The hero film on the virtual clock: vclock.mjs patches HTMLMediaElement play(), pause() and the paused getter, so the page sees the film play (play, playing, pause and ended events) while the element itself stays paused. Each step, vc.media() seeks every playing film to its virtual time only when its 24 fps frame changes, to that frame's centre ((n + 0.5)/24, because WebM's 1 ms timecodes round frame starts), and waits for 'seeked'. It wraps a looping clip, ends the intro so React hands over to the loop, and skips the seek while the hero is off screen. Requests to /videos/ are left out of the quiet() wait, because the loop's open-ended range request never finishes.

Per step:
1. Apply the input.
2. vc.advance(1/240 s, 4.167 ms).
3. Flush the IntersectionObserver with two real rAFs (__vc.real.raf).
4. vc.step(): currentTime = now − birth for every animation.
5. vc.media(): bring the film to its frame.
6. A PNG screenshot through a CDP clip scaled to the DPR (a true 2880×1800), then Lanczos3 JPEGs at q92 4:4:4, 1440 wide, plus full size at q93 through film 2.2.

build_steps: 1. Lock the edit as data. The grid is 112.5 BPM (16 frames per beat, 64 per bar), and every time is an output frame, F(n) = n/30. tools/takes.mjs holds the seven takes with their film↔take offsets, rates, warm-ups and every input event; src/camera.js holds the camera keys and the three cuts; src/edit.js holds every overlay with its in and out times and the takes' holds; tools/cue.mjs derives the audio cue (music/cue.json) from the takes' logs.
